messages:
maya (support): hey security team — need a quick check. Brightline reported a production bug that only reproduces with a ~4 day window; their tenant logs were on standard 14d TTL but we compacted some indexes yesterday. can we pause deletion for brightline-123 for 7 days so we can capture a full run?

Dustin (eng): thumbs up on needing more time. can we instead extract a focused slice (request IDs) so we don't keep full logs?

maya (support): we can try to extract a slice but the errors look tied to cache warmup across many requests, so we probably need the raw traces + request logs for a few hours across the window.

alex (sec): quick questions: 1) Are these logs containing any user-entered PII (names, emails) or auth tokens? 2) Where exactly are the objects stored (s3 bucket + prefix or trace store)?

maya (support): we believe they contain user_ids and email hashes, no plaintext passwords or tokens. stored in s3: s3://redwood-prod-logs/brightline/brightline-123/ and traces in honey-db/brightline-123/ (short-term).

caroline (legal): if email hashes only and no full identifiers, extension might be OK with a documented exception and limited access. Need an access list and justification note for our retention-exception tracker.

alex (sec): agree. security checklist: - scope the copy to only the prefixes we need - run a redaction pass if possible (mask emails/ids) - limit who can access the copied bucket/prefix and timebox IAM permissions - create an exception ticket with justification + owner + expiry.

maya (support): who signs off on the exception? is legal + sec both required?

caroline (legal): legal + sec signoff yes. product or support should request and be owner of the exception.

Dustin (eng): operational suggestion: create a scoped S3 copy to a secure ephemeral bucket and add tag `retention-exception:brightline-123` and lifecycle 7d. infra can set bucket policy to only allow e-2fa groups and the job that copies. example CLI: ```aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-logs/brightline/brightline-123/ s3://redwood-ephemeral/brightline-123/ --recursive --profile infra && aws s3api put-bucket-tagging --bucket redwood-ephemeral --tagging 'TagSet=[{Key=retention-exception,Value=brightline-123}]'```

alex (sec): also add an automated redaction step before copy if possible. if not, we can gate access and run redaction in-place then delete originals if required.

maya (support): action items: 1) maya to file exception ticket with justification + list of request IDs 2) eng (dustin) to create scoped copy with lifecycle 7d and restrict IAM 3) sec (alex) + legal (caroline) to sign off. i'll file ticket now.

sec-bot: retention-exception ticket created: RE-2026-487 with owner maya. please add approvers.

caroline (legal): added approvers: alex, caroline. documented justification looks fine, flag if any PII found during review.

alex (sec): approved pending one condition: run an email-hash-to-anon mapping to avoid linking to external identity providers. then full approval. :white_check_mark:

Dustin (eng): copying now to ephemeral bucket, will DM logs when done.

maya (support): thanks team — will close loop once they've reproduced.

alex (sec): note for records: once ticket expires, infra should verify lifecycle deletion and confirm via a short audit note in RE-2026-487.

maya (support): noted. thanks :pray:
